Ahuka.note: A Yadava patriarch; father of Devaka and Ugrasena.

Devaka.note: Yadava prince, son of Ahuka; father of Devaki.

Ugrasena.note: Yadava king of Mathura, son of Ahuka; deposed by his son Kamsa and restored by Krishna. Kept a virtual prisoner through Kamsa's whole reign of terror; on Kamsa's death Krishna put him back on the throne and himself accepted no kingdom in Mathura, the reason Yadava rule there sits with Ugrasena's house rather than Vasudeva's own.

Kamsa.note: Son of Ugrasena; the tyrant of Mathura who jailed Devaki and Vasudeva and was slain by the young Krishna. A voice at Devaki's wedding warned that her eighth child would kill him; he killed her first six infants for it and would have killed the seventh (Balarama, moved to Rohini's womb) and eighth (Krishna, smuggled to Gokula) in turn. Sent Putana, Trinavarta, Vatsasura and a train of other demons to kill the boy at Gokula, all failed; finally summoned Krishna and Balarama to a wrestling exhibition at Mathura meaning to have them killed in the ring, and was pulled from his own throne and killed by Krishna before the assembly instead.

Devaki.note: Daughter of Devaka, wife of Vasudeva and mother of Krishna; her first sons were killed by her cousin Kamsa.

Shurasena.note: Shura, son of Vidhuratha of the Vrishni house; ten sons, of whom Vasudeva was the chief, and five daughters, one of them Pritha whom he gave to his friend Kunti. The Bhagavata runs his descent through Chitraratha and Vidhuratha, this tree through Vrishni, and both are recorded. SB 9.24.26-28

Vasudeva.note: Son of Shurasena; father of Krishna, Balarama and Subhadra. Imprisoned by Kamsa, he bore the newborn Krishna across the river to safety.

Kunti.note: Also Pritha, daughter of Shurasena, given in fosterage to Kuntibhoja. By name — a mantra from Durvasa that could call any deva to father a child, tested once in girlhood to bear and abandon Karna, then used three times as Pandu's wife to bear Yudhishthira, Bhima and Arjuna (and lent to Madri for Nakula and Sahadeva), Pandu's death beside Madri and her return to Hastinapura with the five boys, surviving Duryodhana's plots at their side, her secret night meeting with Karna before Kurukshetra, and her last years in the forest with Dhritarashtra and Gandhari, dying with them in the fire.

Shrutashrava.note: Daughter of Shurasena, sister of Vasudeva; wed to Damaghosha of Chedi and mother of Shishupala.

Kuntibhoja.note: A childless Bhoja king, cousin of Shurasena; he adopted Pritha, who took his name as Kunti.

Krishna.note: Eighth son of Vasudeva and Devaki, carried across the Yamuna the night he was born and raised by Nanda and Yashoda in Gokula. Of the whole list the Bhagavata sets him apart: krsnas tu bhagavan svayam, the others are portions and portions of portions, and he is the source Himself. The twentieth of the avatars, SB 1.3.23, 1.3.28. Too much story for one note; by name only — Putana, Trinavarta, Shakatasura, Yamalarjuna, Kaliya-damana, the Govardhana lift, the rasa-lila, Akrura's arrival, the Kamsa-vadha, the move to Dvaraka, Rukmini-harana, Jarasandha's seventeen sieges, the Syamantaka jewel, Narakasura-vadha and the sixteen thousand rescued, Shishupala-vadha at Yudhishthira's Rajasuya, Usha-Aniruddha and the war with Bana and Shiva, charioteer at Kurukshetra and speaker of the Bhagavad Gita, Sudama's visit, the Yadava civil war at Prabhasa, and his own end by the hunter Jara's arrow, mistaking his foot for a deer's eye.

Balarama.note: Elder brother of Krishna, carried from Devaki's womb into Rohini's, and counted with him as the nineteenth and twentieth descents, born in the house of Vrishni to take the burden off the earth. He carried the plough and the pestle, taught both Duryodhana and Bhima the mace, and would take neither side in the war. The nineteenth of the avatars, SB 1.3.23.

Subhadra.note: Sister of Krishna, daughter of Rohini; she eloped with Arjuna at Krishna's urging and became the mother of Abhimanyu.

Pradyumna.note: Son of Krishna and Rukmini; a rebirth of Kamadeva, the god of love.

Samba.note: Son of Krishna and Jambavati; his prank on the sages drew the curse that destroyed the Yadava race.

Aniruddha.note: Son of Pradyumna; carried off by Usha, daughter of the asura Bana, and rescued by Krishna.

Vajra.note: Great-grandson of Krishna; after the Yadavas destroyed themselves he was made their king, so the line survived.

Satrajit.note: A Yadava noble, keeper of the Syamantaka gem; father of Satyabhama.

Devabhaga.note: Brother of Vasudeva; father of Uddhava.

Devashravas.note: Brother of Vasudeva, a Vrishni chief.

Anadhrishti.note: Brother of Vasudeva, a Vrishni warrior.

Shrutadeva.note: Sister of Vasudeva and Kunti; mother of Dantavakra.

Shrutakirti.note: Sister of Vasudeva and Kunti; wed to the king of Kekaya.

Rajadhidevi.note: Sister of Vasudeva and Kunti; mother of Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti.

Uddhava.note: Son of Devabhaga; Krishna's cousin, friend and counsellor, to whom Krishna gave his last teaching.

Sini.note: A Vrishni chief; grandfather of the great warrior Satyaki.

Satyaki.note: Yuyudhana, grandson of Sini; a mighty Vrishni warrior, pupil of Arjuna and Krishna's charioteer, who fought for the Pandavas.

Hridika.note: A Vrishni chief; father of Kritavarma.

Kritavarma.note: Son of Hridika, a Vrishni-Bhoja warrior who fought for the Kauravas and survived the war.

Akrura.note: A Yadava elder who bore Krishna and Balarama from Gokula to Mathura; keeper of the Syamantaka jewel for a time. Sent by Kamsa with false honour to fetch the boys to their deaths at the wrestling exhibition, though himself a lifelong devotee overjoyed at the chance to see Krishna, and granted a vision of Vishnu's own form reflected in the Yamuna while bathing on the way; later suspected of hiding the Syamantaka jewel after Prasena's death until its true history with Jambavan came out.

Charudeshna.note: Son of Krishna and Rukmini, a valiant warrior.

people.Kirtiman: One of the first six sons of Devaki and Vasudeva; killed at birth by Kamsa. In one reading, previously one of the six Maruts under a curse, restored to the heavens when Krishna and Balarama freed them from Kalanemi's world. SB 10.1, 10.85.

Already liberated before the curse, by Sankarshana's own teaching, he bore it without complaint, since a self-realised soul has nothing left for death to take.

Shashabindu.note: Yadava emperor of the world, a great mystic who held fourteen jewels; ten thousand wives and a lakh of sons by each. His daughter Bindumati married Mandhata of the solar line, and their two houses meet in her. SB 9.23.31-32

Bindumati.note: Daughter of the Yadava emperor Shashabindu; queen of Mandhata, mother of Purukutsa, Ambarisha and Muchukunda and of fifty daughters. The cleanest marriage between the solar and lunar lines in the Puranas. SB 9.6.38

Bhajamana.note: Son of Satvata. Six sons by two wives: Nimloci, Kinkana and Dhrishti; Shatajit, Sahasrajit and Ayutajit. SB 9.24.7-8

Devavridha.note: Son of Satvata. Of him and his son Babhru the old verse says that Babhru is the best of men and Devavridha the equal of the devas, and that fourteen thousand and sixty-five of their descendants attained liberation by their company. SB 9.24.7-11

Mahabhoja.note: Son of Satvata, an exceedingly religious king, from whom the Bhoja kings descend. SB 9.24.7, 9.24.11

AndhakaY.name: Andhaka
AndhakaY.note: Son of Satvata; four sons, Kukura, Bhajamana, Shuchi and Kambalabarhisha, and from Kukura the line runs to Ahuka, Devaka and Ugrasena. Not Andhaka the Daitya. SB 9.24.7, 9.24.19

BabhruDv.name: Babhru
BabhruDv.note: Son of Devavridha, praised with his father in an old verse. SB 9.24.9-10

Kukura.note: Eldest of Andhaka's four sons, with Bhajamana, Shuchi and Kambalabarhisha. SB 9.24.19

AnuK.name: Anu
AnuK.note: Whose friend was the gandharva Tumburu. SB 9.24.20

Punarvasu.note: A son, Ahuka, and a daughter, Ahuki. SB 9.24.20-21

Ahuki.note: Daughter of Punarvasu, sister of Ahuka. SB 9.24.21

Yudhajit_2.name: Yudhajit
Yudhajit_2.note: Son of Vrishni; father of Shini and Anamitra. Not Yudhajit of Kekaya. SB 9.24.12

Anamitra.note: Son of Yudhajit. Three sons: Nighna, a second Shini, and Vrishni. SB 9.24.12-14

Nighna.note: Son of Anamitra; his sons were Satrajita and Prasena. SB 9.24.12-13

VrishniIII.name: Vrishni
VrishniIII.note: Son of Anamitra, and father of Shvaphalka and Chitraratha. SB 9.24.14

Prasena_2.name: Prasena
Prasena_2.note: Son of Nighna, brother of Satrajit; he wore the Syamantaka jewel to the hunt and was killed by a lion. SB 9.24.13; 10.56

Shvaphalka.note: Son of Vrishni; by his wife Gandini the father of Akrura and twelve more, and a daughter Suchara. SB 9.24.15-18

ChitrarathaV.name: Chitraratha
ChitrarathaV.note: Son of Vrishni, brother of Shvaphalka; his son Viduratha fathered Shura. SB 9.24.15, 9.24.26

Vidhuratha.note: Son of Chitraratha, father of Shura. SB 9.24.26

Dhritadeva.note: Eldest of Devaka's seven daughters, all of whom Vasudeva married. SB 9.24.22-23

Shantideva.note: Daughter of Devaka, wife of Vasudeva. SB 9.24.23

unions.note: Rati, serving Shambara as his cook under the name Mayavati, raised the infant Pradyumna after a fish swallowed him; she recognised him as Kamadeva reborn, and married him once grown, after he killed Shambara. SB 10.55.

SB 9.6.38. Both were already here and her note already said whose daughter she was; the union between them had never been written. Her marriage to Mandhata is the cleanest join in the Puranas between the solar and the lunar houses.
